read.cue: the defence has overloaded to the strong (puck) side, leaving the weak side and net-front open

interaction.prompt: Your winger has the puck on the wall and the defence has collapsed to the puck side. Drag your three teammates into the open, dangerous ice.

feedback.right: You read the overload: with the defence stacked strong-side, the net-front and the weak side are wide open, and your point keeps it in. That's where the danger is.
feedback.wrong: Stacking the strong side just piles into where the defence already is. The defence overloaded the puck, so the open, dangerous ice is the net-front and the weak side.

tip: Read the defence. When they shade to the puck, the open ice is the net-front and the weak side — fill it.
why: Good offensive players attack the space the defence leaves. An overload to the puck opens the net-front and weak side, so that is where the threats belong.
